children: Solana was the only major US spot crypto ETF category to attract new money last week, while Bitcoin and Ethereum funds continued losing billions. However, almost all of Solana’s inflows came from a single day.
According to SoSoValue, Solana ETFs recorded $4.4 million in weekly inflows, ending six consecutive weeks of withdrawals.
Almost all the buying happened on Monday, November 16, when investors poured $11.7 million into Solana funds. Bitwise’s Solana Staking ETF (BSOL) received roughly $10.8 million.
The remaining four trading days brought withdrawals or no inflows.

children: Despite attracting ETF inflows, Solana’s price continued falling. SOL dropped to $65.82 on Friday, losing approximately 13% over seven days.
The altcoin’s next support is near $62. Recovering above $68 could offer some relief.
Meanwhile, Solana ETFs held approximately $965 million in assets on November 20, compared with $1.41 billion in cumulative net inflows since launch.
Although that gap does not directly measure investors’ losses, it reflects the sharp decline in fund asset values.
For now, Solana’s ETF recovery remains fragile. Next week’s flows will reveal whether institutional demand is returning or Monday’s buying was an exception.

title: Solana ETFs Defy Wall Street’s Big Crypto Sell-Off
